newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks seen reacting to scandal news, yen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks seen reacting to scandal news, yen.

text.p: A widening scandal involving the son of President Kim Young-sam and the yen's movement against the dollar would be the twin themes of the South Korean stock market on Tuesday, brokers and analysts said.
"Turmoil, mainly from the political side, would likely suppress investor sentiment," said Kim Myung-ho, market strategist at Hyundai Securities.
The Korea composite price index closed down 6.88 points or 1.01 percent to 672.10 on Monday.

Kim said the market would be influenced by rumours that Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son, was involved in share price manipulation of "many" companies' stocks. About 10 billion won was rumoured to have been involved, he said.
"The feeling is that there will turn out to be something to support these charges," Kim said.

Prosecutors have questioned an associate of Kim Hyun-chul to find out if he accepted kickbacks and reportedly have confirmed that a local construction firm deposited more than one billion won in a bank account suspected of being opened for Kim.
Local media have reported that Kim would soon be arrested.
"This has taken on new dimensions," said Henry Morris, managing director of Coryo International (H.K.) Ltd, a securities firm. "Just when you think it might be put to bed it leaps back out at you."
Hyundai Securities' Kim said he expected Korean stocks to bottom out at about 660 points before turning around.
But renewed strengthening of the yen could prop up Korean share prices, analysts said.
Export-related Korean shares, including heavyweights in the shipbuilding, auto and steel sectors, would rise on the belief that a strong yen would make Korean goods more competitive.
That's what happened on Monday when the yen rose as high as 117.60 to the dollar in early trading in Tokyo.
Two of the three leading shipbuilders, Daewoo Heavy Industries and Samsung Heavy Industries, went limit-up.
Shares of chipmakers Samsung Electronics Co Ltd, Hyundai Electronics Industries Co Ltd and LG Semicon Co rose on the yen and news that global chip prices were set to recover.
"There was a buoyant feeling in the morning, but it's too early to say what the yen is doing," Morris said.
